notes: Root of kumain. Said alone as an invitation; 'Kain tayo' / 'Tara, kain' = let's eat. Polite reply if declining: 'Busog pa po.'

examples.tl: Kain na! Lumalamig na ang ulam.
examples.en: Eat now! The food is getting cold.

examples.tl: Tara, kain muna tayo bago umuwi.
examples.en: Come on, let's eat first before going home.
examples.taglish: Tara, kain muna tayo sa BGC bago umuwi.

notes: Actor-focus um-verb. Aspects: kumain (done), kumakain (now), kakain (will). Object focus is kainin.

examples.tl: Kumain na ba kayo?
examples.en: Have you (all) eaten yet?
examples.taglish: Kumain na ba kayo? Order na tayo kung hindi pa.

examples.tl: Kakain kami sa labas mamaya.
examples.en: We're eating out later.

notes: Object-focus -in form of kain. Aspects: kinain, kinakain, kakainin. 'Kainin mo na' = go ahead and eat it.

examples.tl: Kainin mo na yung tira, masisira pa.
examples.en: Eat the leftovers already, they'll spoil.

examples.tl: Hindi ko kinain yung sili.
examples.en: I didn't eat the chili.

notes: Also means a meal event ('may kainan sa office'). 'Kainan' is any eating place, from carinderia to restaurant.

examples.tl: May bagong kainan sa may Kalayaan, subukan natin.
examples.en: There's a new eatery near Kalayaan, let's try it.

examples.tl: May kainan mamaya sa office, free lunch.
examples.en: There's a meal thing later at the office, free lunch.
examples.taglish: May kainan mamaya sa office, free lunch daw.

notes: Core concept: anything eaten with kanin. 'Ano'ng ulam?' is the daily question. Carinderias display ulam in trays.

examples.tl: Ano'ng ulam natin ngayong gabi?
examples.en: What's our dish for tonight?

examples.tl: Dalawang ulam at isang kanin po.
examples.en: Two dishes and one rice, please.

notes: Cooked rice. Uncooked is bigas; the plant is palay. 'Extra rice' and 'unli rice' are used as-is.

examples.tl: Isa pang kanin po.
examples.en: One more rice, please.

examples.tl: Wala akong kanin, keto ako ngayon.
examples.en: No rice for me, I'm doing keto now.
examples.taglish: No rice ako ngayon, keto kasi.

notes: Sold by the kilo at the palengke or grocery. Kanin once cooked.

examples.tl: Bumili ka ng limang kilo ng bigas sa palengke.
examples.en: Buy five kilos of rice at the market.

notes: Verb: mag-almusal. 'Agahan' is the pure Tagalog synonym; both are heard. Many just say 'breakfast'.

examples.tl: Nag-almusal ka na ba?
examples.en: Have you had breakfast yet?

examples.tl: Tapsilog ang almusal ko lagi sa carinderia.
examples.en: Tapsilog is always my breakfast at the carinderia.

notes: From tanghali (noon). Verb: mananghalian. In Taglish people usually just say 'lunch'.

examples.tl: Saan tayo mananghalian? Sa Glorietta?
examples.en: Where are we having lunch? At Glorietta?

examples.tl: Late na ang tanghalian ko dahil sa meeting.
examples.en: My lunch was late because of the meeting.

notes: From hapon (afternoon/evening). Verb: maghapunan. 'Dinner' is just as common in Taglish.

examples.tl: Ano'ng ulam sa hapunan?
examples.en: What's the dish for dinner?

examples.tl: Mag-dinner tayo sa labas, sawa na ako sa lutong bahay.
examples.en: Let's have dinner out, I'm tired of home cooking.

notes: Spanish loan, a real meal slot around 3-4 PM (and ~10 AM). Verb: mag-merienda. Pancit, turon, halo-halo are typical.

examples.tl: Merienda muna tayo, ang tagal pa ng dinner.
examples.en: Let's have a snack first, dinner is still far off.

examples.tl: Ano'ng merienda ninyo sa office?
examples.en: What's your snack at the office?
examples.taglish: Ano'ng merienda niyo sa office? Pa-order ako.

notes: Noun from kain. 'Foods' as a plural is common Philippine English.

examples.tl: Masarap ang pagkain dito pero mahal.
examples.en: The food here is good but expensive.

examples.tl: May natirang pagkain pa sa ref.
examples.en: There's still leftover food in the fridge.

notes: As a noun = beverage (stress inumín). As a verb inúmin = to drink (object focus). 'Ano'ng inumin mo?' = what will you drink?

examples.tl: Ano'ng inumin niyo? Iced tea o softdrinks?
examples.en: What will you have to drink? Iced tea or soda?

examples.tl: May inumin ba sa package na ito?
examples.en: Does this package include a drink?

notes: Actor-focus um-verb from inom. Aspects: uminom, umiinom, iinom. 'Inom tayo' can also mean let's go drinking (alcohol).

examples.tl: Uminom ka ng maraming tubig, mainit ngayon.
examples.en: Drink lots of water, it's hot today.

examples.tl: Inom tayo sa Poblacion sa Friday.
examples.en: Let's go drinking in Poblacion on Friday.

notes: English root with mag-. Aspects: nag-order, nag-oorder, mag-oorder. 'Order' alone works as an imperative. 'Pa-order' = order for me / I'd like to order.

examples.tl: Nag-order na ako ng Grab Food, darating sa 30 minutes.
examples.en: I already ordered Grab Food, it arrives in 30 minutes.

examples.tl: Mag-order na tayo, gutom na ako.
examples.en: Let's order now, I'm hungry.

notes: 'Pa-' + verb = request to have something done. Follow with 'ng' + item. Used in person and in chat/Viber group orders.

examples.tl: Pa-order po ng isang tapsilog at isang kape.
examples.en: I'd like to order one tapsilog and one coffee, please.

notes: paki- + bigay. Add 'po' for politeness. Follow with 'ng' + thing and 'sa' + person. Also 'pakiabot' (pass, hand over).

examples.tl: Pakibigay po ng toyo.
examples.en: Please give me the soy sauce.

examples.tl: Pakibigay sa kanya yung sukli.
examples.en: Please hand him the change.

en: may I have; please give me
notes: pa- + hingi (ask for). Softer than pakibigay; add 'po' and 'ng'. Used for both free and paid items.

examples.tl: Pahingi po ng tubig.
examples.en: May I have some water, please.

examples.tl: Pahingi ng isang kagat ng burger mo.
examples.en: Give me one bite of your burger.

notes: 'Isa pa po' to the waiter; 'isa pa nga' casual. 'Isa pa' also means 'also/another thing' in conversation.

examples.tl: Isa pa pong kanin.
examples.en: One more rice, please.

examples.tl: Isa pa, ate! Yung beer.
examples.en: One more, miss! The beer.

notes: Standard way to ask for the check in Manila restaurants. Often with a hand gesture of writing in the air. 'Chit' is the older word.

examples.tl: Ate, bill out po.
examples.en: Miss, the bill please.

examples.tl: Bill out na tayo, late na.
examples.en: Let's get the bill, it's late.

notes: Older/colloquial word for the bill, still heard ('Pakikuha ng chit'). Younger staff say 'bill'.

examples.tl: Pakikuha po ng chit.
examples.en: Please bring the bill.

notes: Said as-is. Cashiers ask 'Dine-in or take-out?' Also 'pabalot' for wrapping leftovers.

examples.tl: Take-out po, isang chickenjoy.
examples.en: To go, please, one chickenjoy.

examples.tl: Take-out na lang, wala nang upuan.
examples.en: Let's just take out, there are no more seats.

notes: The standard counter question is 'Dine-in or take-out po?' Answer with either word plus 'po'.

examples.tl: Dine-in po, para sa dalawa.
examples.en: Dine in, please, for two.

en: I'd like to buy (at a counter)
notes: pa- + bili. The opener at a sari-sari store, 7-Eleven or street stall. Follow with 'ng' + item. Also = please buy for me ('Pabili ako ng yelo').

examples.tl: Pabili po ng isang Coke at yelo.
examples.en: I'd like one Coke and ice, please.

examples.tl: Pabili ako ng pandesal pag-uwi mo.
examples.en: Buy me pandesal on your way home.

notes: Only for price (how many = ilan). 'Magkano po?' / 'Magkano lahat?' / 'Magkano kilo?'

examples.tl: Magkano po ang sinigang?
examples.en: How much is the sinigang?

examples.tl: Magkano lahat?
examples.en: How much altogether?

notes: 'Libre ko' = my treat. 'Ilibre mo ako' = treat me. 'Libre' also means free time (libre ka ba bukas?).

examples.tl: Libre ko ngayon, birthday ko kasi.
examples.en: My treat today, it's my birthday.

examples.tl: Libre ang tubig pero bayad ang yelo.
examples.en: The water is free but the ice costs.

notes: Not expected when there is a service charge; small tips are welcome in carinderias and for riders. 'Keep the change' = 'Sa iyo na ang sukli.'

examples.tl: May service charge na, pero nag-iwan pa rin ako ng tip.
examples.en: There's already a service charge, but I still left a tip.

examples.tl: Bigyan mo ng tip yung rider, umulan e.
examples.en: Give the rider a tip, it rained.

notes: Most sit-down restaurants add 10% on top of VAT. Check the receipt before tipping.

examples.tl: May service charge ba dito? Tingnan mo sa resibo.
examples.en: Is there a service charge here? Check the receipt.

en: split the bill; everyone pays their own
notes: Kanya-kanyang bayad. Said when nobody is treating. 'Hati tayo' = let's split evenly.

examples.tl: KKB tayo ha, walang libre.
examples.en: We each pay our own, okay? Nobody's treating.

examples.tl: Hati tayo sa bill, 350 each.
examples.en: Let's split the bill, 350 each.
examples.taglish: Hati tayo sa bill, 350 each, GCash mo sa akin.

notes: 'Hati tayo' = let's split (the bill or the food). 'Kalahati' = a half. 'Paghatian' = share among.

examples.tl: Hati tayo sa isang order ng sisig, malaki e.
examples.en: Let's share one order of sisig, it's big.

notes: 'Gutom na ako' = I'm hungry now. 'Nagugutom ako' = I'm getting hungry. 'Gutom' is also the noun hunger.

examples.tl: Gutom na ako, kain na tayo.
examples.en: I'm hungry, let's eat.

examples.tl: Nagugutom ako kapag naamoy ko ang lechon.
examples.en: I get hungry when I smell lechon.

notes: 'Busog na ako' = I'm full. 'Nakakabusog' = filling. 'Busog pa ako' is the polite way to decline food.

examples.tl: Busog na ako, salamat. Hindi ko na kaya.
examples.en: I'm full, thanks. I can't eat any more.

examples.tl: Nakakabusog ang silog kahit mura.
examples.en: Silog is filling even though it's cheap.

notes: 'Nauuhaw ako' = I'm getting thirsty. 'Nakakauhaw' = makes you thirsty (e.g. maalat na chichirya).

examples.tl: Uhaw ako, pabili ng malamig na tubig.
examples.en: I'm thirsty, let me buy cold water.

notes: 'Unli' = unlimited, used for rice, wings, samgyupsal. 'Extra rice' = one extra serving.

examples.tl: Unli rice dito, kaya sulit.
examples.en: Unlimited rice here, so it's worth it.

examples.tl: Extra rice po, isa.
examples.en: Extra rice please, one.

notes: 'Pakidagdag' = please add more. 'Dagdag bayad' = additional charge. 'Dagdagan mo' = add to it.

examples.tl: Pakidagdag ng sabaw, ate.
examples.en: Please add more soup, miss.

examples.tl: May dagdag na bayad ang extra sauce.
examples.en: Extra sauce has an additional charge.

notes: Ask the server or anyone at the next table. Also 'Ano'ng bestseller niyo?'

examples.tl: Kuya, ano'ng masarap dito? First time ko.
examples.en: Sir, what's good here? It's my first time.

notes: Standard at a carinderia where there's no menu. 'Meron' is the spoken form of mayroon.

examples.tl: Ate, ano pong meron? Wala na bang sinigang?
examples.en: Miss, what do you have? No more sinigang?

notes: 'Ubos na po' = we've run out. 'Naubos' = got used up. 'Ubusin mo' = finish it (all).

examples.tl: Ubos na po ang lechon kawali.
examples.en: The lechon kawali is sold out.

examples.tl: Ubusin mo yung kanin mo, sayang.
examples.en: Finish your rice, it'd be a waste.

notes: From Spanish exacto. 'Sakto lang ang anghang' = the spice is just right. Also means 'just enough money'.

examples.tl: Sakto lang ang alat, hindi sobra.
examples.en: The saltiness is just right, not too much.

notes: 'Patikim' = let me try some / here, try some. 'Tikman mo' = taste it. Common at the palengke for fruit.

examples.tl: Patikim naman ng kare-kare mo.
examples.en: Let me have a taste of your kare-kare.

examples.tl: Tikman mo muna bago ka maglagay ng patis.
examples.en: Taste it first before you add fish sauce.

notes: 'Tira' as a noun = what's left. 'Natira' = was left over. 'Pabalot' to take leftovers home.

examples.tl: Yung tira kagabi, iprito mo lang bukas.
examples.en: Last night's leftovers, just fry them tomorrow.

notes: pa- + balot (wrap). The way to ask for leftovers to be packed. Also used at the counter: 'Pabalot na lang' = make it to go.

examples.tl: Ate, pabalot po itong natira.
examples.en: Miss, please wrap up these leftovers.

examples.tl: Pabalot na lang, kakainin ko sa condo.
examples.en: Just wrap it, I'll eat it at the condo.

notes: Change the number: para sa tatlo, para sa apat. For portions: 'good for two' is used as-is on menus.

examples.tl: Table para sa dalawa po.
examples.en: A table for two, please.

examples.tl: Yung platter, good for two daw.
examples.en: The platter is good for two, they say.

notes: 'Sawa na ako sa manok' = I'm sick of chicken. 'Nakakasawa' = gets tiring. 'Hindi nakakasawa' = never gets old.

examples.tl: Sawa na ako sa Jollibee, iba naman tayo.
examples.en: I'm tired of Jollibee, let's go somewhere else.

examples.tl: Hindi nakakasawa ang adobo.
examples.en: Adobo never gets old.

notes: Cheap, home-style ulam in trays; you point at what you want. 'Turo-turo' is the same idea (turo = point).

examples.tl: Kain tayo sa carinderia, 80 pesos lang ang ulam at kanin.
examples.en: Let's eat at the carinderia, rice and a dish is only 80 pesos.

notes: From turo (point): you point at the dishes in trays. Same as carinderia; slightly more casual term.

examples.tl: Sa turo-turo, tinuturo mo lang yung gusto mong ulam.
examples.en: At a turo-turo, you just point at the dish you want.

notes: pa- + English verb, very common Taglish. 'Mag-Grab Food' also works. Rider = delivery driver.

examples.tl: Pa-deliver na lang tayo, umuulan.
examples.en: Let's just have it delivered, it's raining.

examples.tl: Nandito na daw yung rider sa lobby.
examples.en: The rider is already in the lobby, they say.

notes: Used as a verb too: 'mag-Grab Food', 'nag-Grab ako'. Foodpanda is the other big app.

examples.tl: Mag-Grab Food na lang tayo, tamad akong lumabas.
examples.en: Let's just order Grab Food, I'm too lazy to go out.

examples.tl: Ang mahal ng delivery fee sa Grab ngayon.
examples.en: The delivery fee on Grab is expensive right now.

en: adobo (meat stewed in soy, vinegar, garlic)
notes: The unofficial national dish. Chicken (manok) or pork (baboy). 'Adobong manok', 'adobong baboy'. Keeps well; classic baon.

examples.tl: Adobong manok ang baon ko ngayon.
examples.en: Chicken adobo is my packed lunch today.

examples.tl: Mas masarap ang adobo kinabukasan.
examples.en: Adobo tastes better the next day.

notes: Sour (maasim) soup with pork, shrimp or fish and vegetables. 'Sinigang na baboy', 'sinigang na hipon'. Comfort food on rainy days.

examples.tl: Umuulan, perfect sa sinigang na baboy.
examples.en: It's raining, perfect for pork sinigang.

examples.tl: Pakidagdag ng sabaw ng sinigang.
examples.en: Please add more sinigang broth.

notes: Clear chicken soup with ginger (luya), green papaya or sayote, and malunggay or chili leaves. The go-to when sick.

examples.tl: May sipon ako, tinola ang hanap ko.
examples.en: I have a cold, I'm craving tinola.

notes: Peanut-based stew, usually oxtail and tripe, always served with bagoong on the side. Fiesta/Sunday dish.

examples.tl: Hindi kumpleto ang kare-kare kung walang bagoong.
examples.en: Kare-kare isn't complete without bagoong.

notes: Chopped pork (face/ears), onion, kalamansi, chili, often with egg on a sizzling plate. The number one pulutan.

examples.tl: Isang sisig at dalawang beer, kuya.
examples.en: One sisig and two beers, sir.

examples.tl: Pakilagay ng itlog sa sisig.
examples.en: Please put an egg on the sisig.

notes: Centerpiece of fiestas, Christmas and birthdays. 'Lechon kawali' is deep-fried pork belly, a different dish. 'Lechon manok' = roast chicken.

examples.tl: May lechon sa birthday ni Tita.
examples.en: There's lechon at Auntie's birthday.

examples.tl: Lechon kawali at kanin, tapos sawsawan na Mang Tomas.
examples.en: Lechon kawali with rice, then Mang Tomas sauce.

notes: 'Lumpiang Shanghai' = small fried meat rolls (party staple). 'Lumpiang sariwa' = fresh (unfried). 'Lumpiang gulay/togue' = vegetable rolls.

examples.tl: Laging may lumpiang Shanghai sa handaan.
examples.en: There's always lumpiang Shanghai at a party.

notes: Any noodle dish: pancit canton (stir-fried), bihon (rice noodles), palabok (with orange sauce). Served on birthdays for long life.

examples.tl: Pancit para sa mahabang buhay, birthday ko kasi.
examples.en: Noodles for long life, since it's my birthday.

examples.tl: Pancit canton at itlog, tapos na ang merienda.
examples.en: Instant pancit canton and an egg, that's my snack done.

en: garlic rice + fried egg combo meal
notes: SInangag + itLOG. Add the meat as a prefix: tapsilog, longsilog, tosilog, bangsilog, hotsilog, cornsilog. A 'tapsihan' sells them 24/7.

examples.tl: Ano'ng silog mo? Tapsilog o longsilog?
examples.en: Which silog do you want? Tapsilog or longsilog?

examples.tl: Open 24 hours yung tapsihan sa may corner.
examples.en: The tapsilog place at the corner is open 24 hours.

en: beef tapa, garlic rice, fried egg
notes: TAPa + SInangag + itLOG. The most common silog. Comes with sawsawan of suka and sibuyas.

examples.tl: Isang tapsilog po, over easy yung itlog.
examples.en: One tapsilog please, egg over easy.

notes: LONGganisa + SInangag + itLOG.

examples.tl: Longsilog ang favorite ko, matamis yung longganisa.
examples.en: Longsilog is my favorite, the sausage is sweet.

notes: TOcino + SInangag + itLOG. Sweet cured pork.

examples.tl: Tosilog para sa bata, hindi maanghang.
examples.en: Tosilog for the kid, it's not spicy.

notes: Thin beef marinated in soy, garlic, kalamansi, then fried. The 'tap' in tapsilog. Not the Spanish tapas.

examples.tl: Masarap ang tapa nila, hindi matigas.
examples.en: Their tapa is good, not tough.

notes: Regional styles: sweet (hamonado, e.g. Pampanga) or garlicky-sour (recado, e.g. Vigan, Lucban). Breakfast staple.

examples.tl: Bumili ako ng Vigan longganisa sa palengke.
examples.en: I bought Vigan longganisa at the market.

notes: Red, sweet, cured pork slices, fried for breakfast. Sold in packs in every grocery.

examples.tl: Tocino at sinangag, tapos kape, solb na ang umaga.
examples.en: Tocino and garlic rice, then coffee, and the morning is sorted.

notes: Pritong itlog = fried egg; nilagang itlog = boiled egg; itlog na maalat = salted duck egg (red shell). Also slang for zero/nothing.

examples.tl: Dalawang itlog po, sunny side up.
examples.en: Two eggs please, sunny side up.

examples.tl: Wala na tayong itlog, bili ka sa tindahan.
examples.en: We're out of eggs, buy some at the store.

notes: Common fish: bangus (milkfish), tilapia, galunggong (GG), tuna. 'Pritong isda' = fried fish; 'inihaw na isda' = grilled.

examples.tl: Pritong isda at kamatis, ulam ng probinsya.
examples.en: Fried fish and tomatoes, a provincial meal.

examples.tl: Sariwa pa ba itong isda?
examples.en: Is this fish still fresh?

notes: Also the live bird. 'Pritong manok' = fried chicken; 'inihaw na manok' = grilled; 'lechon manok' = roast chicken.

examples.tl: Manok na lang ulit? Sawa na ako.
examples.en: Chicken again? I'm sick of it.

examples.tl: Isang kilo ng manok, pakihiwa na.
examples.en: One kilo of chicken, please cut it up.

notes: Both the animal and the meat. Liempo = belly, kasim = shoulder, pata = hock. Also slang for messy/greedy.

examples.tl: Baboy o manok ang adobo niyo?
examples.en: Is your adobo pork or chicken?

examples.tl: Hindi ako kumakain ng baboy.
examples.en: I don't eat pork.

notes: Stress matters: báka = cow/beef; bakâ = maybe. 'Karne ng baka' = beef. Bulalo and tapa are beef dishes.

examples.tl: Mahal ang baka ngayon sa palengke.
examples.en: Beef is expensive at the market now.

examples.tl: Baka? Baka hindi, baboy yan.
examples.en: Beef? Maybe not, that's pork.

notes: 'Sinigang na hipon', 'halabos na hipon' (steamed in salt water). Say 'allergic ako sa hipon' if needed.

examples.tl: Allergic ako sa hipon, may hipon ba dito?
examples.en: I'm allergic to shrimp, is there shrimp in this?

notes: Inihaw na pusit (grilled stuffed squid) and calamares (fried rings) are common pulutan.

examples.tl: Order tayo ng inihaw na pusit, pampulutan.
examples.en: Let's order grilled squid as bar food.

notes: 'Ginisang gulay' = sauteed vegetables; 'lumpiang gulay'. 'Vegetarian' is said in English.

examples.tl: Kain ka ng gulay, hindi puro karne.
examples.en: Eat vegetables, not just meat.

examples.tl: May gulay lang ba kayo na ulam? Vegetarian ako.
examples.en: Do you have a vegetable-only dish? I'm vegetarian.

notes: Sold by the kilo at the palengke or from a cart. Ask 'Hinog na ba?' (is it ripe?).

examples.tl: Bumili tayo ng prutas pang-dessert.
examples.en: Let's buy fruit for dessert.

notes: Hinog (ripe, yellow) or hilaw (green, eaten with bagoong). Guimaras and Cebu mangoes are famous. 'Mango' is also said.

examples.tl: Manggang hilaw at bagoong, favorite ko.
examples.en: Green mango with bagoong, my favorite.

examples.tl: Magkano kilo ng mangga?
examples.en: How much per kilo of mangoes?

notes: Varieties: lakatan (sweet yellow), latundan, saba (cooking banana, used in turon and banana cue).

examples.tl: Saging ang baon ko para sa gym.
examples.en: I packed a banana for the gym.

notes: Mature coconut, grated for gata (coconut milk) and kakanin. Young coconut for drinking is buko.

examples.tl: May gata ng niyog ang laing at Bicol express.
examples.en: Laing and Bicol express have coconut milk.

notes: Drinking coconut. Buko juice, buko pandan (dessert), buko pie (Laguna). Sold fresh from carts and 7-Eleven.

examples.tl: Pabili ng buko juice, ang init.
examples.en: Let me buy coconut juice, it's so hot.

examples.tl: Pasalubong na buko pie galing Laguna.
examples.en: Buko pie from Laguna as a homecoming gift.

notes: Tiny sour citrus squeezed into sawsawan, pancit, sisig, and juice. 'Kalamansi juice' is on most menus.

examples.tl: Pigain mo ang kalamansi sa pancit.
examples.en: Squeeze the kalamansi onto the noodles.

examples.tl: Isang kalamansi juice, walang asukal.
examples.en: One kalamansi juice, no sugar.

notes: Stress: sukà = vinegar, súka = vomit. Used in adobo, paksiw, and as dip with garlic and chili (sukang may sili).

examples.tl: Pahingi ng suka para sa chicharon.
examples.en: Give me some vinegar for the pork rinds.

notes: Toyo + kalamansi = toyomansi, the all-purpose dip. 'May toyo' also slangily means someone is acting crazy.

examples.tl: Toyo at kalamansi ang sawsawan ng inihaw.
examples.en: Soy sauce and kalamansi is the dip for grilled food.

notes: Salty fermented fish sauce. Seasoning for sinigang, tinola, and as a dip with kalamansi and sili.

examples.tl: Lagyan mo ng kaunting patis ang sinigang.
examples.en: Put a little fish sauce in the sinigang.

notes: Bagoong alamang (shrimp) goes with kare-kare and green mango; bagoong isda is for pinakbet. Strong smell, strong love.

examples.tl: Ang bagoong ay para sa kare-kare at manggang hilaw.
examples.en: Bagoong is for kare-kare and green mango.

notes: 'Maalat' = salty. 'Pakiabot ng asin' at the table. Rock salt is used for itlog na maalat.

examples.tl: Kulang sa asin yung sabaw.
examples.en: The soup needs more salt.

notes: Whole peppercorns (buong paminta) go in adobo. Bell pepper is 'bell pepper'; chili is sili.

examples.tl: Lagyan mo ng buong paminta ang adobo.
examples.en: Put whole peppercorns in the adobo.

notes: 'Walang asukal' = no sugar. 'Matamis' = sweet. Coffee shops ask 'sugar level?' in English.

examples.tl: Kape na walang asukal, gatas lang.
examples.en: Coffee with no sugar, just milk.

examples.tl: Ubos na ang asukal, bili ka sa Seven.
examples.en: We're out of sugar, buy some at 7-Eleven.

notes: 'Mamantika' = oily/greasy. Sold tingi in small bags at sari-sari stores.

examples.tl: Sobrang mamantika ang pritong manok nila.
examples.en: Their fried chicken is very greasy.

examples.tl: Pabili ng mantika, pang-prito.
examples.en: Buy cooking oil, for frying.

notes: From sawsaw (to dip). Toyomansi, suka with garlic, Mang Tomas, bagoong. Diners mix their own.

examples.tl: Ano'ng sawsawan mo sa lumpia? Suka o sweet chili?
examples.en: What's your dip for lumpia? Vinegar or sweet chili?

examples.tl: Pakilagay ng sawsawan sa take-out.
examples.en: Please include dipping sauce with the take-out.

notes: From pulot (pick up). Sisig, chicharon, mani, inihaw. 'Pampulutan' = something to serve as pulutan.

examples.tl: Ano'ng pulutan natin? Sisig at chicharon?
examples.en: What's our bar food? Sisig and pork rinds?

notes: Umbrella word: puto, kutsinta, suman, bibingka, biko, sapin-sapin. Sold at the palengke and as pasalubong.

examples.tl: Bumili ng kakanin si Lola para sa merienda.
examples.en: Grandma bought rice cakes for the afternoon snack.

notes: Literally 'mix-mix'. Shaved ice, milk, beans, jellies, ube, leche flan. Summer staple; Chowking and Razon's are popular.

examples.tl: Ang init! Halo-halo tayo sa Chowking.
examples.en: It's so hot! Let's get halo-halo at Chowking.

examples.tl: Haluin mo muna bago kainin.
examples.en: Mix it first before eating.

en: warm silken tofu with syrup and sago
notes: Sold by the magtataho shouting 'Tahooo!' in the morning. Served in a cup, 20-30 pesos. Also in 7-Eleven now.

examples.tl: Tumawag ka sa magtataho, gusto ko ng mainit na taho.
examples.en: Call the taho vendor, I want warm taho.

notes: Saba banana (and sometimes langka) in a lumpia wrapper, fried with caramelized sugar. Street merienda, 15-25 pesos.

examples.tl: Pabili ng dalawang turon, merienda ko.
examples.en: Two turon please, my afternoon snack.

notes: Sold at night by vendors calling 'Baluuut!'. Eaten with salt or spiced vinegar. Penoy is the unfertilized version.

examples.tl: Try mo ang balut, may asin at suka.
examples.en: Try the balut, with salt and vinegar.

notes: Slightly sweet rolls sold hot from bakeries at dawn. Dipped in coffee; filled with kesong puti, palaman, or Spam.

examples.tl: Bili ka ng pandesal sa panaderya, mainit pa.
examples.en: Buy pandesal at the bakery, it's still hot.

examples.tl: Pandesal at kape, almusal ng bayan.
examples.en: Pandesal and coffee, the nation's breakfast.

notes: General word for bread. Sliced loaf is often just 'tasty' (from a brand). Panaderya = bakery.

examples.tl: Wala na tayong tinapay para sa almusal.
examples.en: We have no more bread for breakfast.

notes: Leftover rice fried with garlic. The 'si' in silog. 'Fried rice' is also understood.

examples.tl: Gawin nating sinangag ang tirang kanin.
examples.en: Let's make the leftover rice into garlic fried rice.

notes: Plain rice porridge; arroz caldo (with chicken, ginger) and goto (with tripe) are the loaded versions. Sick-day and late-night food.

examples.tl: Lugaw at tokwa't baboy, tapos kape.
examples.en: Rice porridge with tofu and pork, then coffee.

notes: Lugaw with chicken, ginger, safflower, fried garlic and kalamansi. Rainy-day and sick-day food.

examples.tl: Lagnat ako kahapon, arroz caldo ang kinain ko.
examples.en: I had a fever yesterday, I ate arroz caldo.

notes: Beef shank and marrow boiled for hours. Famous in Tagaytay; a cold-weather and drinking food.

examples.tl: Bulalo sa Tagaytay, worth it ang byahe.
examples.en: Bulalo in Tagaytay, the trip is worth it.

notes: Grilled (inihaw na liempo) or fried (lechon kawali). Sold by the kilo at the palengke.

examples.tl: Inihaw na liempo at kanin, tapos toyomansi.
examples.en: Grilled pork belly with rice, then soy-kalamansi dip.

notes: Crispy fried pork skin, dipped in spiced vinegar. Also chicharon bulaklak (intestine). Classic pulutan.

examples.tl: Chicharon na may suka, pulutan natin.
examples.en: Pork rinds with vinegar, our bar snack.

notes: From dugo (blood). Dark savory stew, eaten with puto. Jokingly called 'chocolate meat' to foreigners.

examples.tl: Dinuguan at puto, classic combo.
examples.en: Dinuguan and puto, a classic combo.

notes: Pork, chilies, bagoong and gata. One of the few genuinely spicy Filipino dishes. Laing is the vegetable cousin.

examples.tl: Maanghang talaga ang Bicol express nila, ingat.
examples.en: Their Bicol express is really spicy, careful.

notes: Ilocano dish: squash, eggplant, okra, bitter gourd, string beans, with bagoong and often pork or bagnet.

examples.tl: Pinakbet ang gulay ko ngayon, may ampalaya.
examples.en: Pinakbet is my vegetable dish today, it has bitter gourd.

notes: National fish. Boneless bangus is sold marinated (daing na bangus) for frying. Bangsilog = bangus silog.

examples.tl: Daing na bangus, sinangag at itlog: bangsilog.
examples.en: Marinated milkfish, garlic rice and egg: bangsilog.

notes: Literally 'dry'. Smelly when fried, loved with sinangag, kamatis and suka. Not for the condo kitchen if neighbors complain.

examples.tl: Bawal magprito ng tuyo sa condo, umaamoy sa hallway.
examples.en: Frying dried fish is banned in the condo, it smells up the hallway.

notes: 'Walang sibuyas' = no onions. Red onions are the default; 'sibuyas Tagalog' = small red shallots.

examples.tl: Walang sibuyas po sa burger ko.
examples.en: No onions on my burger, please.

notes: Base of almost every dish (gisa = saute in garlic, onion, tomato). Fried garlic bits top lugaw and sinangag.

examples.tl: Maraming bawang ang sinangag nila, masarap.
examples.en: Their garlic rice has lots of garlic, delicious.

notes: Sliced raw tomatoes with salt or bagoong are a side for fried fish and tuyo.

examples.tl: Pritong tuyo at kamatis, tapos sinangag.
examples.en: Fried dried fish and tomatoes, then garlic rice.

notes: Siling labuyo = tiny very hot chili. Siling haba = long green mild chili. 'May sili ba?' = does it have chili?

examples.tl: May sili ba ito? Hindi ako kumakain ng maanghang.
examples.en: Does this have chili? I don't eat spicy food.

examples.tl: Lagyan mo ng sili ang suka.
examples.en: Put chili in the vinegar.

notes: Purple yam used in halaya (jam), halo-halo, ice cream, and the ube-cheese pandesal craze.

examples.tl: Ube cheese pandesal, uso pa ba yan?
examples.en: Ube cheese pandesal, is that still trendy?

notes: Sold roasted or fried with garlic (adobong mani) by street vendors. Base of kare-kare sauce.

examples.tl: Pabili ng mani sa manong, pampulutan.
examples.en: Buy peanuts from the vendor, for bar snacks.

notes: Kesong puti = fresh white carabao cheese, eaten with pandesal. 'Cheese' is said just as often.

examples.tl: Pandesal na may kesong puti, galing Laguna.
examples.en: Pandesal with white cheese from Laguna.

notes: Chinese-Filipino steamed bun: asado (sweet pork) or bola-bola (meatball with egg). Sold hot at 7-Eleven and Chowking.

examples.tl: Isang siopao asado, pang-merienda.
examples.en: One asado siopao, for a snack.

notes: Pork dumplings with toyo, kalamansi and chili garlic oil. 'Siomai rice' is a cheap meal; sold at stalls and malls.

examples.tl: Siomai rice na lang ako, 60 pesos.
examples.en: I'll just have siomai rice, 60 pesos.

notes: Fried on a cart, speared with a stick, dipped in sweet, spicy or vinegar sauce. Kwek-kwek (orange battered quail eggs) and kikiam share the cart.

examples.tl: Fishball at kwek-kwek sa labas ng school, 5 pesos each dati.
examples.en: Fishball and kwek-kwek outside the school, 5 pesos each back then.

notes: Street barbecue skewer, dipped in vinegar. Other skewers: betamax (blood), adidas (chicken feet), helmet (head).

examples.tl: Isaw at betamax, ihaw-ihaw sa kanto.
examples.en: Isaw and betamax, grilled skewers on the corner.

notes: Filipino barbecue = sweet soy-marinated pork on sticks, grilled. 'Ihaw-ihaw' = street grill stand. Also inihaw.

examples.tl: Tatlong stick ng barbecue at isang kanin.
examples.en: Three sticks of barbecue and one rice.

notes: Small white steamed cakes, often with cheese on top. Partner of dinuguan. Careful: means something else in Spanish.

examples.tl: Puto't dinuguan sa handaan.
examples.en: Puto and dinuguan at the party.

en: rice cake baked in clay pot (Christmas)
notes: Sold outside churches during Simbang Gabi (December), topped with butter, cheese, itlog na maalat and niyog.

examples.tl: Bibingka at puto bumbong pagkatapos ng Simbang Gabi.
examples.en: Bibingka and puto bumbong after the dawn mass.

notes: 'Tubig lang po' = just water. Restaurants ask 'service water or bottled?' Mineral = bottled water in local usage.

examples.tl: Tubig lang po, service water.
examples.en: Just water please, tap/service water.

examples.tl: Pabili ng isang malamig na tubig, 500ml.
examples.en: One cold water, 500ml, please.

notes: 'Magkape tayo' = let's have coffee. 3-in-1 sachets at home, barako from Batangas, Starbucks/Bo's in malls. 'Kapeng mainit' = hot coffee.

examples.tl: Kape muna ako bago mag-work.
examples.en: Coffee first before I work.

examples.tl: Magkape tayo sa Bo's mamaya?
examples.en: Coffee at Bo's later?
examples.taglish: Coffee tayo sa Bo's mamaya? Libre ko.

notes: Most people say 'tea' or the specific drink (iced tea, milk tea). 'Salabat' = ginger tea. Iced tea is the default restaurant drink.

examples.tl: Mainit na tsaa para sa sipon.
examples.en: Hot tea for a cold.

examples.tl: Milk tea na lang ako, less sugar.
examples.en: I'll just have milk tea, less sugar.

notes: 'May gatas' = with milk. Condensed milk (condensada) and evaporated milk are pantry staples for coffee and desserts.

examples.tl: Kape na may gatas, walang asukal.
examples.en: Coffee with milk, no sugar.

examples.tl: Ubos na ang gatas ng bata.
examples.en: The kid's milk is finished.

notes: Said in English. Popular: buko juice, kalamansi juice, mango shake, 'juice' also covers powdered Tang-style drinks.

examples.tl: Anong juice meron? Mango o pineapple?
examples.en: What juice do you have? Mango or pineapple?

notes: Always 'softdrinks', even for one. Coke is the default; 'Coke' can mean any cola. Sold in glass bottles (bote) and 'mismo' small bottles.

examples.tl: Softdrinks na lang ako, Coke Zero kung meron.
examples.en: I'll just have a soda, Coke Zero if you have it.

notes: Everyone says 'beer'; serbesa is the old Spanish word (San Miguel's full name). Order: 'Isang Pale, kuya.' Red Horse is the strong one.

examples.tl: Dalawang San Mig Light, malamig ha.
examples.en: Two San Mig Lights, cold ones okay.

examples.tl: Beer tayo mamaya sa Poblacion?
examples.en: Beers later in Poblacion?

notes: Any alcoholic drink, especially hard liquor (gin, brandy like Emperador, rum like Tanduay). 'Inom' = drinking session.

examples.tl: Hindi ako umiinom ng alak, driver ako ngayon.
examples.en: I don't drink alcohol, I'm the driver tonight.

notes: 'Walang yelo' = no ice. 'Maraming yelo' = lots of ice. Ice is sold in bags at sari-sari stores and 7-Eleven.

examples.tl: Iced tea po, walang yelo.
examples.en: Iced tea please, no ice.

examples.tl: Pabili ng yelo para sa inuman.
examples.en: Buy ice for the drinking session.

notes: Ask for a glass with your bottle: 'May baso po?' or 'Sa baso po'. 'Sa tasa' = in a cup; 'sa bote' = in the bottle.

examples.tl: Yung Coke, sa baso po, may yelo.
examples.en: The Coke in a glass please, with ice.

notes: Temperature only; spicy-hot is maanghang. 'Mainit pa' = still hot. Also for weather: 'Ang init!'

examples.tl: Mainit pa yung pandesal, bagong luto.
examples.en: The pandesal is still hot, fresh from the oven.

examples.tl: Ingat, mainit ang sabaw.
examples.en: Careful, the soup is hot.

notes: 'Malamig na tubig' = cold water. 'Lumamig na' = it got cold. 'Pampalamig' = a cold refreshment.

examples.tl: May malamig na beer ba kayo?
examples.en: Do you have cold beer?

examples.tl: Lumamig na ang pizza, painitin mo.
examples.en: The pizza got cold, heat it up.

notes: Traditionally one shared glass passed around the table (tagayan). 'Tagay!' = drink up / cheers. 'Tagayan mo siya' = pour him one.

examples.tl: Tagay! Para sa bagong trabaho mo.
examples.en: Cheers! To your new job.

notes: The most used food word. 'Sarap!' alone. 'Ang sarap!' = so good. 'Hindi masarap' is the polite 'bad'. Also used for feelings (masarap matulog).

examples.tl: Ang sarap ng sinigang dito!
examples.en: The sinigang here is so good!

examples.tl: Masarap ba yung bagong ramen place sa Salcedo?
examples.en: Is the new ramen place in Salcedo good?
examples.taglish: Masarap ba yung new ramen place sa Salcedo? Try natin.

notes: From asin/alat. 'Sobrang maalat' = too salty. 'Alat' is the noun (saltiness).

examples.tl: Medyo maalat yung tapa pero okay lang.
examples.en: The tapa is a bit salty but it's fine.

notes: Filipino spaghetti, longganisa and tocino are all matamis. 'Tamis' = sweetness. 'Panghimagas' = dessert (formal; people say dessert).

examples.tl: Masyadong matamis ang spaghetti ng Jollibee para sa akin.
examples.en: Jollibee's spaghetti is too sweet for me.

notes: Sinigang and green mango are maasim. 'Asim' = sourness. 'Pa-asim' = make it more sour.

examples.tl: Gusto ko maasim talaga ang sinigang.
examples.en: I like my sinigang really sour.

notes: 'Maanghang ba?' is the key question before ordering. 'Anghang' = spiciness. 'Hindi maanghang' = not spicy. Levels: mild/medium/spicy in English.

examples.tl: Maanghang ba ito? Hindi ako kaya ng maanghang.
examples.en: Is this spicy? I can't handle spicy.

examples.tl: Pakibawasan ng anghang, konting sili lang.
examples.en: Please make it less spicy, just a little chili.

notes: Ampalaya (bitter gourd) is the classic mapait food. 'Pait' = bitterness; also used for heartbreak.

examples.tl: Mapait ang ampalaya pero masarap sa itlog.
examples.en: Bitter gourd is bitter but good with eggs.

notes: Rich, deep, satisfying taste (umami). 'Linamnam' = that savory quality. Used in food ads and by titos describing broth.

examples.tl: Malinamnam ang sabaw ng bulalo, matagal na pinakuluan.
examples.en: The bulalo broth is savory, it was boiled a long time.

notes: For meat = tender; for bread = soft. 'Lambot' = softness. Opposite: matigas.

examples.tl: Malambot ang baka, hindi chewy.
examples.en: The beef is tender, not chewy.

notes: Tough meat, stale bread, hard rice. 'Matigas ang ulo' = stubborn (idiom).

examples.tl: Matigas yung tapa, parang goma.
examples.en: The tapa is tough, like rubber.

notes: Lechon skin, chicharon, fried chicken. 'Lutong' = crunch. 'Crispy' is used just as much.

examples.tl: Malutong pa ang balat ng lechon, sarap!
examples.en: The lechon skin is still crispy, delicious!

notes: Literally brave. For coffee or liquor = strong. Barako coffee is matapang. Opposite for drinks: matabang (weak/bland).

examples.tl: Matapang ang kape dito, hindi ako makakatulog.
examples.en: The coffee here is strong, I won't be able to sleep.

notes: Needs salt or patis. Also = weak coffee. 'Tabang' = blandness. Not to be confused with mataba (fat).

examples.tl: Matabang yung sabaw, lagyan mo ng patis.
examples.en: The soup is bland, add some fish sauce.

notes: Unripe fruit (manggang hilaw) or undercooked food. Opposite: hinog (ripe) / luto (cooked).

examples.tl: Hilaw pa yung kanin, dagdagan mo ng tubig.
examples.en: The rice is still undercooked, add water.

examples.tl: Hinog na ba ang mangga o hilaw pa?
examples.en: Is the mango ripe yet or still green?

notes: 'Ano'ng lasa?' = what does it taste like? 'Lasang ...' = tastes like ... 'Walang lasa' = tasteless. 'Lasahan mo' = taste it.

examples.tl: Lasang pizza yung chichirya na ito.
examples.en: These chips taste like pizza.

examples.tl: Ano'ng lasa ng ube? Parang matamis na kamote.
examples.en: What does ube taste like? Like a sweet potato.

notes: mag- verb from luto. Aspects: nagluto, nagluluto, magluluto. Object focus: lutuin (lutuin mo ang kanin). 'Luto na' = it's cooked/ready.

examples.tl: Magluto tayo mamaya imbes na mag-Grab.
examples.en: Let's cook later instead of ordering Grab.

examples.tl: Sino'ng nagluto nito? Ang sarap!
examples.en: Who cooked this? It's delicious!

notes: From prito (Spanish frito). 'Pritong manok/isda/itlog' before a noun; 'magprito' = to fry; 'iprito mo' = fry it. 'Pinirito' = was fried.

examples.tl: Pritong itlog at sinangag, mabilis lang.
examples.en: Fried egg and garlic rice, it's quick.

examples.tl: Iprito mo na lang yung tirang adobo.
examples.en: Just fry the leftover adobo.

notes: From ihaw (grill). 'Inihaw na liempo/pusit/isda'. 'Ihaw-ihaw' = street grill. 'Mag-ihaw tayo' = let's grill (condo rooftop BBQ).

examples.tl: Inihaw na liempo at toyomansi, tapos kanin.
examples.en: Grilled pork belly with soy-kalamansi, then rice.

examples.tl: Mag-ihaw tayo sa roof deck sa Sunday.
examples.en: Let's grill on the roof deck on Sunday.

notes: From laga (boil). 'Nilagang baka' = boiled beef soup with potatoes and cabbage; 'nilagang itlog' = boiled egg. Clear, mild, comforting.

examples.tl: Nilagang baka ang ulam, may repolyo at patatas.
examples.en: Boiled beef soup is the dish, with cabbage and potatoes.

notes: Gisa = saute. The base step of most Filipino dishes. 'Ginisang gulay/monggo/corned beef'. 'Igisa mo' = saute it.

examples.tl: Ginisang corned beef at sibuyas, ulam ng wala nang budget.
examples.en: Sauteed corned beef and onions, the end-of-budget meal.

notes: Any frying pan. 'Lechon kawali' = pork belly fried in a kawali. Non-stick = non-stick.

examples.tl: Initin mo muna ang kawali bago ilagay ang mantika.
examples.en: Heat the pan first before adding the oil.

notes: Big pot for rice or soup. Kaserola = casserole/saucepan. Rice cooker is said in English.

examples.tl: Nasa kaldero pa ang sinigang, painitin mo.
examples.en: The sinigang is still in the pot, heat it up.

notes: Filipinos eat with spoon and fork (kutsara at tinidor), spoon in the right hand. 'Kutsarita' = teaspoon.

examples.tl: Pahingi po ng kutsara at tinidor.
examples.en: May I have a spoon and fork, please.

examples.tl: Isang kutsaritang asukal lang.
examples.en: Just one teaspoon of sugar.

notes: Partner of the spoon. Chopsticks = chopsticks. Eating with hands = kamayan (boodle fight).

examples.tl: Walang tinidor sa take-out, nakalimutan nila.
examples.en: There's no fork in the take-out, they forgot.

notes: Table or kitchen knife. Rarely on a Filipino table since the spoon does the cutting. 'Pakihiwa' = please cut/slice.

examples.tl: Mapurol ang kutsilyo, hindi makahiwa ng kamatis.
examples.en: The knife is dull, it can't slice a tomato.

notes: Pinggan is the Tagalog synonym, also common ('maghugas ng pinggan'). 'Platito' = saucer/small plate.

examples.tl: Isa pang plato po, mag-share kami.
examples.en: One more plate please, we're sharing.

examples.tl: Ikaw ang maghuhugas ng plato mamaya.
examples.en: You're washing the dishes later.

notes: Glass for drinks. 'Isang basong tubig' = a glass of water. 'May baso po?' when you get a bottle.

examples.tl: Isang basong tubig lang, salamat.
examples.en: Just a glass of water, thanks.

notes: Cup with a handle. 'Isang tasang kape' = a cup of coffee. Also a measuring cup in recipes (1 tasa ng bigas).

examples.tl: Dalawang tasa ng bigas para sa apat na tao.
examples.en: Two cups of rice for four people.

notes: Everyone says 'ref'. 'Pridyider' (from Frigidaire) is old-fashioned. 'Ilagay mo sa ref' = put it in the fridge. Freezer = freezer.

examples.tl: Ilagay mo sa ref yung tira, baka mapanis.
examples.en: Put the leftovers in the fridge, they might spoil.

examples.tl: Wala nang laman ang ref, grocery na tayo.
examples.en: The fridge is empty, let's do groceries.

notes: Gas stove = kalan; LPG tank = tangke/gasul. Many condos have induction ('induction' is said as-is). 'Patayin mo ang kalan' = turn off the stove.

examples.tl: Patayin mo ang kalan, kumukulo na.
examples.en: Turn off the stove, it's boiling already.

examples.tl: Induction lang ang kalan sa condo, bawal ang gasul.
examples.en: The condo stove is induction only, LPG isn't allowed.

notes: 'Dirty kitchen' = outdoor/secondary kitchen for frying and grilling (Philippine English). 'Kusinero/a' = cook.

examples.tl: Maliit ang kusina sa condo pero okay na.
examples.en: The condo kitchen is small but it's fine.

notes: Literally 'house-cooked'. Carinderias advertise 'lutong bahay'. 'Lutong Pinoy' = Filipino cooking.

examples.tl: Miss ko na ang lutong bahay, puro Grab ako buong linggo.
examples.en: I miss home-cooked food, I've been on Grab all week.

notes: Hugas = wash (things, hands). Laundry is labahan. 'Ikaw na maghugas' = you do the dishes. Household rule: the one who cooks doesn't wash.

examples.tl: Ako nagluto, ikaw na maghugas ng plato.
examples.en: I cooked, you wash the dishes.

notes: magpa- + init. Object focus: painitin mo (heat it). Taglish: 'pa-heat mo'. At 7-Eleven: 'Pakiinit po' = please microwave it.

examples.tl: Painitin mo yung ulam sa microwave, isang minuto.
examples.en: Heat up the dish in the microwave, one minute.

examples.tl: Pakiinit po yung siopao.
examples.en: Please heat up the siopao.

notes: The standard 7-Eleven / Ministop request for ready meals. Staff will also ask 'Painitin po?'

examples.tl: Pakiinit po itong rice meal, tapos isang kutsara.
examples.en: Please heat this rice meal, and one spoon.

notes: Everyone says 'Seven'. On every Makati corner: siopao, hot rice meals, coffee, beer, bills payment, GCash cash-in. Ministop and Alfamart are the others.

examples.tl: Daan muna tayo sa Seven, bibili ako ng tubig.
examples.en: Let's stop by 7-Eleven first, I'll buy water.

examples.tl: Open 24/7 ang Seven sa baba ng condo, sulit.
examples.en: The 7-Eleven below the condo is open 24/7, so handy.

notes: Fresh meat, fish, vegetables, fruit by the kilo. Go early. 'Mamalengke' = to go marketing. Haggling (tawad) is normal; having a suki helps.

examples.tl: Mamalengke tayo nang maaga, sariwa pa ang isda.
examples.en: Let's go to the market early, the fish is still fresh.

examples.tl: Mas mura sa palengke kaysa sa grocery.
examples.en: It's cheaper at the market than at the grocery.

notes: From tinda (goods for sale). Usually a small neighborhood store. 'Tindera/tindero' = shopkeeper (f/m). 'Nagtitinda' = sells.

examples.tl: Bili ka ng yelo sa tindahan sa kanto.
examples.en: Buy ice at the store on the corner.

notes: Tiny home-front store selling tingi: single sachets, cigarettes by the stick, cold drinks, load. Often with a window grille. Backbone of barangay life.

examples.tl: May sari-sari store sa tabi ng building, open hanggang 11.
examples.en: There's a sari-sari store next to the building, open till 11.

notes: Two-way loyalty: you're the vendor's suki and they're yours. Gets you better prices, extra pieces and credit. Vendors call anyone 'suki' to be friendly.

examples.tl: Suki na ako sa manok vendor, laging may dagdag.
examples.en: I'm a regular at the chicken vendor, there's always extra.

examples.tl: Suki, bili ka na, mura lang!
examples.en: Hey regular, buy some, it's cheap!

en: retail in small portions; by the piece
notes: Buying one sachet of shampoo, one egg, one cigarette, a small bag of oil. 'Tingi-tingi' = in bits. Sari-sari stores run on tingi.

examples.tl: Tingi lang ang bili ko ng kape, tatlong sachet.
examples.en: I only buy coffee by the sachet, three sachets.

examples.tl: May tingi kayong mantika?
examples.en: Do you sell cooking oil in small portions?

notes: 'Sukli po' = your change (said by cashier). 'Wala pong sukli' = no change available. 'Sa iyo na ang sukli' = keep the change.

examples.tl: Kuya, kulang yung sukli ko.
examples.en: Sir, my change is short.

examples.tl: Sa iyo na ang sukli, salamat.
examples.en: Keep the change, thanks.

notes: 'Pahingi ng resibo' or 'May resibo?' 'OR' = official receipt (for reimbursement). Check for service charge on it.

examples.tl: Pahingi po ng resibo, ire-reimburse ko.
examples.en: Receipt please, I'll get reimbursed.

notes: Plastic = plastic bag. Many Metro Manila cities restrict plastic bags, so stores charge for paper or offer eco bags. 'May plastic?' also works.

examples.tl: Pa-plastic po, marami akong dala.
examples.en: A bag please, I'm carrying a lot.

examples.tl: Wala pong plastic, bawal sa Makati. Paper bag lang.
examples.en: No plastic bags, they're banned in Makati. Only paper bags.

notes: What a cashier, jeepney driver or taho vendor asks when you hand over a 1000. Reply: 'Wala, sorry' or 'Meron, teka'. Carry barya.

examples.tl: Wala kang barya? Wala akong sukli sa isang libo.
examples.en: Don't you have smaller bills? I can't change a thousand.

notes: Coins and small bills. Essential for jeeps, sari-sari stores and street food. 'Pabarya' = please break this bill.

examples.tl: Pabarya ng isang libo, pambayad sa jeep.
examples.en: Please break this thousand, for the jeepney fare.

examples.tl: May barya ka ba? Pambili ng taho.
examples.en: Do you have coins? To buy taho.

notes: 'Bayad po' when handing money. 'Magbayad' = to pay. 'Bayaran mo' = pay for it. 'Bayad na' = already paid. 'Kanya-kanyang bayad' = KKB.

examples.tl: Bayad po, dalawang tapsilog.
examples.en: Here's payment, two tapsilog.

examples.tl: Bayad na ba yung Grab? Cash o GCash?
examples.en: Is the Grab paid already? Cash or GCash?

notes: GCash (and Maya) QR payments work at most stalls and carinderias now. Look for the QR Ph sign. 'Scan lang po' = just scan.

examples.tl: Pwede GCash? Wala akong cash.
examples.en: Can I pay with GCash? I don't have cash.

examples.tl: Scan lang po dito, tapos ipakita ang confirmation.
examples.en: Just scan here, then show the confirmation.

notes: 'Pwede pa-tawad?' / 'Tawad naman' = can you give a discount? 'Tumawad' = to haggle. Works at the palengke, not at 7-Eleven. Also = forgiveness in church.

examples.tl: Ate, tawad naman, tatlong kilo kukunin ko.
examples.en: Miss, give me a discount, I'm taking three kilos.

examples.tl: Pwede pa-tawad? Last price na ba yan?
examples.en: Can you lower it? Is that your last price?

notes: Stress: múra = cheap; murá = to curse. 'Ang mura!' = so cheap. 'Mas mura' = cheaper. 'Murang-mura' = very cheap.

examples.tl: Ang mura ng ulam dito, 70 lang.
examples.en: The dishes here are so cheap, only 70.

examples.tl: Mas mura sa palengke, pero mas malinis sa grocery.
examples.en: Cheaper at the market, but cleaner at the grocery.

notes: Also means 'love' (mahal kita). 'Ang mahal!' = so expensive. 'Masyadong mahal' = too expensive. BGC prices are mahal.

examples.tl: Ang mahal ng kape sa BGC, 250 isang cup.
examples.en: Coffee in BGC is so expensive, 250 a cup.

examples.tl: Masyadong mahal, sa carinderia na lang tayo.
examples.en: Too expensive, let's just go to the carinderia.

notes: um-verb from bili. Aspects: bumili, bumibili, bibili. Object focus: bilhin (bilhin mo). 'Bili ka ng...' = go buy...

examples.tl: Bumili ako ng prutas sa palengke kanina.
examples.en: I bought fruit at the market earlier.

examples.tl: Bili ka ng itlog at pandesal sa Seven.
examples.en: Go buy eggs and pandesal at 7-Eleven.

notes: 'Mag-grocery' = to do grocery shopping. SM Supermarket, Landers, S&R, Robinsons. 'Grocery' means both the store and the trip.

examples.tl: Mag-grocery tayo sa SM mamaya, wala nang laman ang ref.
examples.en: Let's do groceries at SM later, the fridge is empty.

examples.tl: Mahal mag-grocery sa Landers pero bulk.
examples.en: Groceries at Landers are expensive but you buy in bulk.
